forensic_summary.trigger: The EVT2 build faced a 'Kill' scenario with a 100% mechanical retention failure (7/7 units 'stuck in Bazooka') and a critical safety failure where the cosmetic 'Air Gap' switch failed to break the 120V circuit consistently (BAZ-81). Simultaneously, tolerance analysis revealed a 0.3mm interference in the slide-lock mechanism due to 'pillowing' from square tooling dimples.
forensic_summary.intervention: The Architect mandated a 'Stop Ship' on the ID-driven round button, forcing a reversion to a functional square 'TEST' button to meet UL 1472. He orchestrated the '3Tabs concept' structural redesign to resolve the wiggle/stuck interface issues and directed a tooling change from square dimples to 'circular pips' to flatten the chassis.
forensic_summary.result: Secured UL safety compliance, eliminated the 0.3mm interference, and achieved passing thermal metrics (<60°C touch temp).

scars.label: The '3Tabs' Intervention
scars.description: Resolved catastrophic 100% failure rate (7/7 units stuck) by re-architecting internal latching structures.

scars.label: UL 1472 Safety Stop
scars.description: Mandated regression to square 'TEST' button geometry to pass 100-cycle high-voltage endurance test.

scars.label: Tooling Deformation Check
scars.description: Replaced square stamping dimples with circular pips to eliminate 'pillowing' and restore 0.3mm fit clearance.

scars.label: Thermal 'Hot Box'
scars.description: Engineered 850W thermal extraction in enclosed chassis, resolving capacitor failure and acoustic buzzing.

scars.label: Grounding Paradox
scars.description: Balanced conductivity vs oxidation risk by optimizing laser etch area on die-cast housing.
